subject: Strategy anchors + OKR commitment checkpoint for Q3 kickoff
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strategy anchors + OKR commitment checkpoint for Q3 kickoff

Team —

I'm sending the current OKR matrix (attached) and a short set of anchors we want to lock before the QBR dry run next week. High level asks:

- Confirm owners for each objective (comment in the spreadsheet).
- Confirm primary metric and measurement rubric for the top 5 objectives.
- Flag any resource blockers (capacity, infra, or headcount) by EOD so we can route to finance/ops.

Quick context: EdgeScale pilot KPIs and the Dedicated capacity ramp are going to be the anchor for the Platform and Reliability objectives. If we can't commit on capacity ramp dates today, we'll need fallback measures for QBR (see row 3 of the matrix).

Attachments: Q2_OKR_matrix.xlsx (matrix + owner cols)

Notes for replies: please be brief — a one-line commit + one-line blocker is ideal. I'll collate and move to leadership sign-off once we have alignment.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:05:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy anchors + OKR commitment checkpoint for Q3 kickoff

On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> I'm sending the current OKR matrix (attached) and a short set of anchors we want to lock before the QBR dry run next week.

Thanks Naomi — quick responses inline below and a small attachment with suggested measurement updates.

- Owner confirmations: I can own Platform Objective 1 (Model latency reduction) but would like Marcus as the ops co-owner for capacity-related tasks.
- Metric change suggestion: for Objective 2 (Throughput economics) propose switching to p50 cost-per-1k-tokens rather than avg cost — it better reflects production behavior. See measurement_rubric_v2.xlsx attached.
- Blockers: none immediate, but we need a clearer rollback/fallback if the Dedicated ramp slips. Add an explicit fallback milestone (QBR fallback flag).

Short answer: commit if Marcus confirms the capacity dates.

—Grace
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy anchors + OKR commitment checkpoint for Q3 kickoff

Naomi / Grace —

Agree with Grace's metric tweak. Quick updates from infra/ops:

- Dedicated capacity ramp: current procurement and infra prep timeline supports a soft ramp starting 2027-07-18, full ramp by 2027-08-08 if no supply hiccups.
- Blockers: we need 160 GPU-hours/week reserved across two clusters for the first 6 weeks of the ramp; without that we cannot guarantee p50 latency targets.
- Proposed mitigation: we can keep a soft fallback to hosted model-variant with aggressive prefix caching for the first two weeks of the ramp (will preserve latency for 60% of traffic). See capacity_runbook.pdf for runbook.

Action: Karthik, can you confirm whether we have the budgeted GPU-hours to reserve? If not, we need a prioritized list of KR work to delay.

-Marcus
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy anchors + OKR commitment checkpoint for Q3 kickoff

Marcus —

Short answer on capacity: we currently have a partial commit in the Dedicated budget, but not the full 160 GPU-hours/week reservation. Two options:

1) Approve an on-demand top-up for the first 4 weeks (cost delta estimated ~$18k) — procurement can fast-track if Naomi signs off.
2) Defer the lower-priority KR in Objective 2 (embedding cache expansion) to prioritize capacity for latency KRs.

I'll need a one-line decision before 16:00 PT to make the procurement call today. If we go with option 1, procurement will prepare PO docs and loop in EdgeScale finance (miriam.lopez@edgescale.com) for pilot cost-sharing where applicable.

-Karthik
VP, Engineering Finance & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership request: OKR anchors + procurement decision for QBR prep (please sign off)

Hannah —

Summary for leadership sign-off (short):

- Owners: Grace (Platform Obj 1), Marcus (ops co-owner), Naomi (strategy lead) — owners updated in attached matrix.
- Metric: adopt p50 cost-per-1k-tokens for Throughput economics (Grace proposal).
- Capacity ask: reserve 160 GPU-hours/week for the first 6 weeks of ramp. Procurement options: on-demand top-up (~$18k) or defer lower-priority KR.
- External: EdgeScale has indicated willingness to cost-share pilot uplift; procurement will coordinate with miriam.lopez@edgescale.com.

Attachments: Q2_OKR_matrix.xlsx, measurement_rubric_v2.xlsx, capacity_runbook.pdf, qbr_dryrun_agenda.pdf

Request: sign-off on the capacity top-up (option 1) or approval to defer the embedding cache KR (option 2). We need a decision by EOD to keep the QBR playbook intact.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-playbook
Jira: JIRA-OPS-1245 (capacity reservation work)

If approved, I'll publish the finalized slide deck and schedule a 30-min pre-QBR dry run with the owners and EdgeScale next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Strategy
Redwood Inference

Approved.

- Proceed with option 1 (on-demand top-up) to avoid shifting scope before the QBR.
- Karthik: please fast-track procurement and confirm PO docs by EOD.
- Naomi: schedule the dry-run and include the qbr_dryrun_agenda.pdf in invites.

Thanks —
